checks.finding: tasks.md T-001/T-002 (Risk: high) touch B1, a critical-tier gate's process-lifecycle boundary (Risk Rationale, tasks.md:126-141, 240-246); scope is real code (run-panelist-*.sh/.ps1), not doc/CSS-only, so no over-classification. T-003 (Risk: low, tasks.md:317-324) and T-004/T-005 (Risk: medium, tasks.md:375-382, 430-436) are documentation-only with no auth/authz/payment/PII/migration/API-contract surface touched, so low/medium is consistent with the policy's own tier definitions. No issues found.

T-001 Done-When (tasks.md:215-228) and T-002 Done-When (tasks.md:295-307) each carry a two-stage TDD Red->Green evidence item and an independent-review-verdict-plus-QG-verdict item recorded by a named reviewer distinct from the implementing agent. No task is Risk: critical, so second-approver/signature evidence is not required. No issues found.

specs/epic-136-phase4-docs/tasks.md:173-228 (T-001 Done-When) contains 14 distinct verifiable checklist items (mechanically counted via grep), and tasks.md:272-307 (T-002 Done-When) contains 10 — both exceed the '>8 distinct verifiable items' oversizing indicator (T-001 by 75%). Items span config parsing/validation (AC-003), three independent timeout sub-cases (AC-004 a/b/c), a no-verdict fail-closed assertion (AC-005), downstream gate-composition (AC-006), a portability constraint, a default-sourcing constraint, regression preservation, a diff-verified untouched-file constraint (BL-002), plus TDD and independent-review evidence, bundled into one commit-scoped task. Bundling this many independently-checkable claims raises the risk that the required independent review samples rather than exhaustively verifies each one -- the same omission failure mode acceptance-tests.md's own Notes section (citing epic-136-phase3's FP-02) warns against.

T-001/T-002 map to AC-003 (invalid-config error path: 0/-5/abc exit 2) and AC-004 sub-cases (b)/(c) (SIGTERM-ignoring escalation, polling-boundary race) per acceptance-tests.md:38-77 -- edge/error paths, not happy-path only. T-003 is itself a failure-taxonomy documentation task (AC-001/AC-002, requirements.md:21-39). T-004's AC-008 (acceptance-tests.md:105-107) is an explicit anti-padding edge-case assertion. T-005's AC-009/AC-014 require documenting surfaces with no mitigation (residual risk) as an explicit edge case (requirements.md:123-141). No functional task is happy-path-only. No issues found.

Each task's declared Test Type matches acceptance-tests.md's own Test Matrix and the definitions: T-001/T-002 'integration' (tasks.md:149-156, 254-255) involve >=2 real components (runner + stub CLI child process, plus check-cross-model for AC-006), correctly distinguishing AC-003's unit-tier sub-cases within the same suite. T-003/T-004/T-005 'integration (real file read)' matches acceptance-tests.md:7-20's Test Matrix and the repo's own documented convention (acceptance-tests.md:126). No mismatch found.

T-001 (tasks.md:163-171) and T-002 (tasks.md:262-270), the only Risk: high tasks, each carry an explicit Rollback field describing single-commit revert, that it is not a neutral undo (reopens B1 DoS per infra-spec.md Rollback), and required companion-revert coordination (T-001 with T-003's taxonomy; T-002's PowerShell/POSIX parity asymmetry). No issues found.

tasks.md:81-102 (Global Constraints) discloses that all five tasks add cases to the same two shared test suites, and T-004/T-005 additionally share docs/THREAT-MODEL.md. This overlap is fully serialized by a linear Blockers chain (tasks.md:161,260,339,395,449), which transitively prevents any concurrent edit of a shared file. Matches the check's 'legitimate multi-task scope sharing... provided Blockers enforces ordering' allowance. No uncoordinated overlap found.

Each Blockers edge is explicitly labelled and justified in tasks.md:91-102: T-002<-T-001 (functional + shared-artifact), T-003<-T-002 and T-004<-T-003 (shared-artifact only, disclosed honestly), T-005<-T-004 (functional). No edge lacks a stated justification, and no cross-task dependency is left undeclared. No spurious or missing blockers found.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. T-001 through T-005 are new-capability (timeout bound) and documentation-completion tasks, not scoped as bugfix, regression fix, debugging, or incident remediation.
